sources.title: Roadmap for Artificial Intelligence Safety Assurance, Version I
sources.inspection_scope: Inspected the complete 31-page FAA PDF, Version I. Relevant passages: foreword; pp. 3-5 (purpose, principles and stated industry-method gap); pp. 7-11 (existing ecosystem and learned-versus-learning distinction); pp. 12, 24-30 (consensus standards, research and project-specific path discussion).

regions.locator: PDF physical p. 6 / printed p. 5, introduction
regions.excerpt: The industry lacks a method for the safety assurance of AI.

regions.locator: PDF physical p. 11 / printed p. 10, learned AI implementation and update discussion
regions.excerpt: each new version is subjected to safety assurance

regions.locator: PDF physical p. 12 / printed p. 11, project-specific engagement
regions.excerpt: using project-specific issue papers that can be tailored to each project

regions.locator: PDF p. 14, application of principles to aircraft certification safety assurance of learned AI implementations
regions.excerpt: The unique characteristic of AI is that the implementation is learned, rather than designed.

sources.limitations: This 2024 roadmap is a living direction-setting document, not a binding means of compliance, type certificate, TSO authorization, or approval of a particular trained model. Its statement about the industry-method gap is date-bound and cannot establish that no qualifying method now exists.

sources.title: EASA Concept Paper: Guidance for Level 1 & 2 Machine Learning Applications, Issue 02
sources.inspection_scope: Inspected the complete 285-page Issue 02 PDF. Relevant passages: pp. 4-6 (purpose, non-definitive status and approval-use qualification); pp. 8-9 (AI assurance, explainability and residual-risk framing); p. 50 onward (learning assurance objectives, not independently reinterpreted here).

regions.excerpt: does not constitute at this stage definitive or detailed guidance

regions.locator: PDF p. 5, use of guidance pending IRs or AMC
regions.excerpt: facilitating the preparation of the approval or certification
does not constitute in itself any warranty of fitness to obtain a final EASA approval

sources.limitations: Issue 02 is EASA concept guidance for Level 1 and Level 2 ML applications, not definitive detailed guidance, an AMC, or an approval decision. Its document status requires separate treatment from the later Proposed Issue 03 and from any completed RMT.0742 output.

sources.title: EASA Concept Paper: Guidance for Safety-Related Artificial Intelligence Applications — Proposed Issue 03
sources.inspection_scope: Inspected the complete 239-page Proposed Issue 03 PDF and EASA publication metadata. Relevant passages: pp. 4-6 (status, scope, anticipated means of compliance and disclaimer); table of contents for coverage of AI assurance, advanced automation, risk mitigation and organisational provisions.

regions.excerpt: does not constitute at this stage definitive or detailed guidance

regions.locator: PDF p. 6, anticipated means of compliance
regions.excerpt: not considered as either a complete or a binding set of means of compliance
does not constitute in itself any warranty of fitness to obtain a final EASA approval

sources.limitations: The title and text identify this as Proposed Issue 03. It supplies a rich set of candidate objectives and anticipated MOC but no final binding EASA AI certification basis. It cannot be presented as final rulemaking or proof that a given advanced-automation system satisfies approval requirements.

sources.title: ISO/PAS 8800:2024 — Road Vehicles — Safety and Artificial Intelligence
sources.inspection_scope: Inspected ISO's public product page, public abstract, lifecycle and edition/status metadata. The 172-page licensed text was not acquired or inspected.

regions.locator: ISO public page, status and edition metadata
regions.excerpt: Publicly Available Specification ... Published (Edition 1, 2024)
Examples of AI elements within the vehicle include the trained AI model
construct a convincing safety assurance claim for the absence of unreasonable risk

sources.limitations: ISO/PAS 8800 is a published Publicly Available Specification for a stated road-vehicle scope, not an aviation regulation or a disclosed product-assurance result. The licensed text, clauses, conformity mechanism and any real operator's conformance evidence remain uninspected.

sources.title: ANSI/UL 4600, Standard for Evaluation of Autonomous Products, Edition 3
sources.jurisdiction: ANSI/UL autonomous-product safety arguments; voluntary consensus standard
sources.inspection_scope: Captured and inspected UL’s public product page, Edition 3 status, ANSI approval date and public scope summary. The licensed full standard and proposal text were not acquired.

regions.excerpt: ACTIVE ... ANSI Approved: March 17, 2023
building and evaluating a safety argument for vehicles that can operate in an autonomous mode
necessary, but possibly not sufficient, level of completeness and rigor

sources.limitations: The active consensus standard is not a government approval, does not prove a particular vehicle conforms, and its public scope explicitly leaves completeness/rigor conditional. A CSDS proposal dated August 2026 is a proposed revision, not evidence that Edition 3 has changed.

sources.title: Automated Driving Systems — NHTSA current operating guidance page
sources.jurisdiction: US federal motor-vehicle safety; ADS Levels 3-5 guidance
sources.inspection_scope: Inspected NHTSA's current Automated Driving Systems page and its ADS 2.0 discussion, including stated current-operating-guidance status, voluntary/no-approval boundaries and the twelve safety elements.

regions.excerpt: no compliance requirement or enforcement mechanism

regions.locator: NHTSA page, current guidance and approval statement
regions.excerpt: assessments are not subject to Federal approval
Operational Design Domain (ODD) ... Object and Event Detection and Response (OEDR) ... Fall Back

sources.limitations: The page describes ADS 2.0 as NHTSA's current operating guidance, but it is a voluntary policy originating in 2017 and does not supply a frozen-model certification criterion. Later NHTSA activity must be checked separately rather than inferred from this page.

sources.title: Trump’s Transportation Department Cuts Red Tape to Safely Fast-Track Automated Vehicle Innovation
sources.jurisdiction: US federal motor-vehicle safety and automated vehicles
sources.inspection_scope: Inspected the complete NHTSA announcement, including its stated temporary Zoox exemption, A2SCEND performance-standard-development initiative, planned updated guidance and Part 555 description.

regions.excerpt: Accelerate development of first-ever AV performance standards
temporary exemption ... up to 2,500 vehicles annually for two years
updating its technical guidance for AVs for the first time since 2017

sources.limitations: This is an authority announcement of initiatives and a limited exemption, not the future performance standards, updated technical guidance, a general vehicle approval, or disclosure of a learned model's evidence. It creates a time-sensitive tension with the older ADS 2.0 page, which an integrator must reconcile at publication time.
